findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O errors (missing file, permission denied, truncated file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing filesystem input aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain error enum) and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value and on overflow beyond u32 range
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (non-numeric second field) causes a panic instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .trim().parse::<u32>().map_err(...) and propagate the error through a Result return type

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy widening-to-narrowing cast. Values > 65535 silently truncate to u16 range
findings.failure_mode: integer overflow silently corrupts the stored value (e.g. 70000u32 becomes 4464u16), violating data integrity with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(...) to detect and reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(..).collect() builds an intermediate Vec for a two-field record. Holzman requires split_once for single-separator extraction
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line, and the Vec length is never validated so out-of-bounds access follows
findings.fix: replace with line.split_once(',').ok_or(…) to extract name and value fields without intermediate allocation

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexed access into a heap-allocated Vec of unknown length
findings.failure_mode: empty or single-element lines cause a panic at runtime (index out of bounds)
findings.fix: use split_once and .ok_or(...) to require exactly two fields at compile-protected sites

findings.problem: parts[1] is unchecked indexed access into a Vec of unknown length
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one comma-separated field panic at runtime on index out of bounds
findings.fix: use the second binding from split_once(_, ',') instead of index-1 access

findings.problem: load_batchs is an I/O function (fs::read_to_string, println!) that returns a plain Vec with no error type, violating the imperative shell boundary
findings.failure_mode: side effects (filesystem reads, console writes) are mixed into the function signature with no way for callers to handle failures or distinguish core from shell
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, AppError>, remove println! (logging belongs in the shell), and let the caller decide I/O policy

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effecting log call in a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: pollutes stdout with implementation details, breaks testability, and couples the pure-seeming data structure to a concrete logging mechanism
findings.fix: remove println! entirely or push it into a shell-layer wrapper that decides logging policy

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity pre-allocation on the result Vec. The function grows a Vec from unknown line counts with no bounded allocation handling
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation on large files with no graceful handling of AllocationError; repeated reallocations degrade performance
findings.fix: use Vec::with_capacity hint or try_reserve with AllocationError handling if the caller can supply a line count estimate

findings.problem: No benchmark exists to measure the hot path of load_batchs. The intermediate Vec allocation and per-line String allocations have no measured alternative
findings.failure_mode: unverified performance claim; switching to split_once + string slices (borrowed) could be faster but is unmeasured
findings.fix: add a criterion or minicomp benchmark for load_batchs before and after applying split_once + borrowed slices

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_batchs performance
no profiler data for allocation hotspots in the batch loader
no allocation analysis (try_reserve or capacity budget) evidence
no command-level evidence (cargo fmt / cargo clippy / cargo test) was run
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The function has 8 BLOCKER-level violations covering panic-unsafe unwrap calls, unchecked indexing, lossy as casts, missing Result propagation, split_once violations, and I/O in a data-loading path. All must be fixed before delivery.
